newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair promotes Singapore freight route.
newsitem.headline: Swissair promotes Singapore freight route.

text.p: Next week Swissair Cargo is making a marketing push to airport officials, forwarders, shippers and customs officials of its new Singapore freighter service, a Swissair official said.
Since the start of winter timetables on October 27, Swissair has operated a twice-weekly McDonnell DC10-30F service between Geneva and Singapore.
The aircraft, which carries an average of 67 tonnes of cargo per flight, is being wet-leased from U.S. operator, Gemini Air Cargo.

The head of Swissair Cargo, Peter Somaglia, will host the presentation In Geneva on November 13 which will include a tour of cargo-handling installations at the airport, and is designed to show that Swissair now has direct freighter links from Geneva with the Far East and South America, with Geneva now the gateway for its weekly DC10-30F service to Sao Paulo. The service had been launched from Basle in September 1996.

"Given that the aircraft on the Singapore route is the the same as that for Sao Paulo, we thought it was both an economic and ecological choice to base it in Geneva thus doing away with the need for ferry flights to and from Basel," the spokesman added. - Air Cargo Newsdesk Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
